tasks.instruction: Implement rotate(grid, turns) in tiles.py to rotate a grid counter-clockwise. The grid is a list of rows (lists) of equal length. Rotate it by 90 degrees counter-clockwise, turns times; turns is any integer, negative turns rotate the other way and only turns modulo 4 matters. Return a new list of lists and do not modify the input. An empty grid ([]) or a grid of empty rows is returned unchanged as a new list. Raise ValueError if the rows have different lengths. Save tiles.py.

Fix versions.py: sort_versions(versions) must sort version strings. Each version is a string of dot-separated non-negative integers like "1.10.2". Compare part by part as integers (so "1.10" is newer than "1.9") and return a new list ordered oldest first (ascending). Missing trailing parts count as 0, so "1.2" and "1.2.0" are equal versions. Equal versions are ordered by their string, in the same direction. Raise ValueError for an empty string or any non-numeric part. Write the result to versions.py.

A shorter version that is a prefix of a longer one is older, so "1.2" comes before "1.2.0". Equal versions are ordered by their string, in the same direction. Raise ValueError for an empty string or any non-numeric part. Write the result to releases.py.

In spiral.py, write spiral(matrix) that should unwind a matrix in spiral order. The matrix comes as a list of equally long lists, one per line. Begin in the top-left corner and move inwards in a spiral, clockwise: first along the top line to the right, then down the right edge, and so on until every element has been taken exactly once. Return all elements in the order visited as one flat list. For [] or a matrix whose lines are empty the answer is []. If the lines differ in length, raise ValueError. Save the file spiral.py.

In timespan.py, write duration_value(text) that should convert a duration text to a number. A duration is one or more parts written as a non-negative integer followed by a unit: d (days), h (hours), m (minutes), s (seconds), for example "1d2h" or "90m15s". Return the total number of seconds as an int. Spaces between the parts are allowed and ignored ("1h 30m"). The units must appear from largest to smallest and each at most once. Raise ValueError for an empty text, a missing number, an unknown unit, a repeated unit or units in the wrong order. Save the file timespan.py.

Return the total number of whole minutes (leftover seconds are dropped) as an int. Spaces between the parts are allowed and ignored ("1h 30m"). The units must appear from largest to smallest and each at most once. Raise ValueError for an empty text, a missing number, an unknown unit, a repeated unit or units in the wrong order. Write the result to durations.py.
